text: dsh-lark-bridge 是把飞书接入 DSH 的消息通道，让你在私聊或群聊中驱动 agent 处理工作。它通过飞书长连接接收消息，为不同聊天建立会话，并把思考过程、工具结果、审批卡片和最终答复发回聊天。用户还可搜索历史会话、切换模型、查看余额，并在运行中补充或调整任务。首次启动可扫码注册飞书应用；适合希望从飞书远程使用本机 DSH 工作区的人。需要飞书应用和 DSH 环境。

dsh-lark-bridge connects Feishu chats to DSH agents. Messages drive per-chat sessions; progress, tool results, approvals, and replies return to chat. Users can search history, switch models, check balance, and steer tasks. QR onboarding can register a Feishu app. Requires Feishu and DSH.

dsh-lark-bridge 的功能「聊天驱动 agent」：在飞书私聊或群聊中发送消息即可驱动 DSH agent，并将回复送回原聊天。
dsh-lark-bridge 的功能「扫码注册」：未配置应用凭证时启动飞书应用注册流程，在终端显示二维码供飞书扫码完成授权。
dsh-lark-bridge 的功能「聊天命令」：提供历史会话搜索、余额查询、模型切换和帮助等命令，便于直接在聊天中管理 agent。
dsh-lark-bridge 的功能「任务过程回传」：把 agent 的思考过程、工具调用和审批交互呈现在飞书消息中，并回传最终结果。

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🤔 What it does：**Who it's for** — someone with one laptop, who works over Feishu, and wants an AI agent to touch their real files. No server, no ops, no public URL.

**What it replaces** — the loop of *open the IDE → describe the task → watch it edit → switch back to chat to report*. That loop becomes one sentence in Feishu.

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🤔 What it does：**Why not another bridge** — most Feishu-agent bridges hand you a bot that answers messages. This hands you an agent with a terminal, approval gates and session memory — and it shares the same session library as your DSH Desktop, so work begun in the chat is still there when you open the desktop app.

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🧭 How it works：- **In** — the message arrives over a WebSocket long connection. No callback URL, no reverse proxy, no public IP.
- **Through** — the bridge maps each chat (DM or group) to its own `dsh` agent, which reads and writes your real working directory.
- **Back** — thinking, approval requests and results return to the chat as native Feishu messages.
- **Shared** — the `web` and `desktop` runtime forms share one `~/.dsh` session library.

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🧭 How it works：A cloud ledger keyed per endpoint (`deviceId` + `form` + `profile`) keeps one instance per endpoint answering and elects a successor when the active one goes quiet. Both forms read and write the same sessions, so failing over never loses the conversation.

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · Runs on your machine, in minutes, with no public address：One `pnpm dlx` command installs the plugin and boots the host; a QR code is the whole credential flow. The transport is an outbound WebSocket long connection — nothing has to reach you from the internet.
section: Runs on your machine, in minutes, with no public address

text: @moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · You can see what it's thinking：Reasoning renders as Feishu's own *thinking* message. Tool calls arrive with their icon and the first lines of their result; the full output stays in the session log. Every turn closes with one plain line — how many tool calls it made, how long it took. Nothing has to be taken on faith.
section: You can see what it's thinking

text: @moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · A long task is not "fire and forget"：Send a message while a turn is running and it follows `busyPolicy`: `queue` waits its turn, `steer` takes over at the next step boundary **without discarding work already done**, `inject` adds context without waking the driver. Risky operations become approval cards. Turn on `autoResumeGoals` and a goal picks itself back up after a restart.

That's it.：- **Use `pnpm`, not `npx`.** On one machine this was recorded at about 20 seconds versus about 25 minutes (npm's serial reify), and on a ≤4 GB machine the npm process died with "JavaScript heap out of memory" mid-install. Those are the author's numbers, not a benchmark this repository reproduces — treat the gap as *large*, not as *exactly 20 vs 25*.
- **Do not `npm i -g dsh-lark-bridge`.** That name on npm belongs to an unrelated project. This one is **`@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge`**.

After the failed install pnpm writes the literal text `set this to true or false` there — replace it with `false`. Then **re-run the same command**: a failed install leaves the profile half-configured (bundles are not merged when the install exits non-zero), so editing the file alone does not finish the job.

<details>
<summary>📦 Moving to a new machine</summary>

The bridge carries its own migration path. On the old machine:

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：```text
/bot export include-secrets --to-feishu   # uploads to the app's own Feishu drive
/bot export include-secrets               # or a local file, credentials masked
```

The Feishu route needs no copying: the file lands in the app's own cloud space, and the new machine pulls it with `/bot import --from-feishu`. For the local route, copy the printed file to the same path on the new machine, install the plugin there, then:

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：```text
/bot import                       # preview: settings + plugin plan + warnings
/bot import apply                 # execute (add --from-feishu for the cloud slot)
```

What travels: shared settings and per-profile plugin lists. What never travels: peer heartbeats, control tokens, `node_modules`, session history.

Session history lives under `~/.dsh`. To carry it across, copy the session directories **only**:

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：```text
~/.dsh/sessions/     # the conversations themselves
~/.dsh/storages/     # session projection cache and workspace index
```

**Do not copy the whole of `~/.dsh`.** `~/.dsh/dsh-lark-bridge/device-state.json` holds this machine's `deviceId` and its retired flag — a copy would give the new machine the old machine's identity (both would answer the same chat) and could carry the retired flag along.

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：**Device lifecycle** — every machine mints a stable `deviceId` on first boot; `/bot devices` shows the roster. Instead of stopping the old service by hand, retire it: `/bot retire` puts it out of the reply path (messages get a one-line notice, not an agent turn); `/bot activate` brings it back. Every live machine renews its presence each minute, and if the active one goes silent, the freshest endpoint with the lowest endpoint key wins the election on the next inbound message. `/bot name <readable-name>` names a device for the roster.

<details>
<summary>❓ FAQ</summary>

<details>
<summary>Do I need a public IP or webhook?</summary>

No. The transport is a WebSocket long connection; the app must use long-connection event subscription (self-built app).

</details>

<details>
<summary>I have DSH Desktop and the web host — will they both answer?</summary>

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：No. Both share one `~/.dsh` session library, and cloud arbitration is keyed per endpoint (`deviceId:form:profile`): exactly one instance replies per endpoint at any moment, and if the active one goes silent the freshest endpoints elect a successor on the next message. `/bot devices` shows who.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Which models work?</summary>

Any model routable by your dsh deployment — the bridge is model-agnostic, and `/model` switches at runtime.

</details>

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：<details>
<summary>The agent says it sent a file but nothing arrives</summary>

File delivery is default-deny: configure `outbound.allowedFileDirs`. URLs and raw buffers always work.

</details>

<details>
<summary>The web console returns 401 when I open it directly</summary>

Each launch mints a new token, so a browser without the cookie gets 401. Open the full `http://127.0.0.1:18787/?token=…` URL the launcher prints once — that sets a long-lived cookie, after which the plain address works.

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：</details>

<details>
<summary>The slash panel is empty or partial after a restart</summary>

Boot registers constant commands; the full panel sync runs on the first message of a session. Send the bot anything. If it stays empty, check the `application:app_slash_command` scope and publish an app version.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How do I switch to a different Feishu app?</summary>

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：`/bot account save <name>` archives the current credentials; later `/bot account` and tap **Use** on the card, then `/restart` (web) or restart Desktop. Multiple credential sets can live side by side.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What survives a restart?</summary>

Sessions resume from their logs; permission and preset choices ride with the session state. Active goals re-arm only if you set `autoResumeGoals: true` (it defaults to false).

</details>

</details>

@moyu-good/dsh-lark-bridge README · 🎯 Three commands to try first：- **The desktop form lacks question cards.** `hostQuestions` is not available in the `desktop` runtime form; the `web` form is unaffected.
- **Transport-level config is read once at startup.** Credentials, `requireMention` and allowlists need a restart; other config edits hot-reload via dsh's Config-only HMR (`/config` shows live values).
- **Events during a long-connection outage are not replayed** (no cursor); outbound sends are queued by the replay port.
- **`schedule_*` model tools** need `@deepseek-ai/dsh-schedule` composed in your profile.
- **File sending is deny-by-default** — directories must be listed in `outbound.allowedFileDirs` first.
- **Two processes sharing one endpoint key will both answer.** Arbitration compares the endpoint key (`deviceId` + `form` + `profile`); a `dsh web` process and a bare CLI process on the same machine and profile produce the same key, so neither sees the other as a rival. Run one host process per profile.
